questions.question: Which topology connects all devices to a central device?
questions.explanation: In a star topology, all network nodes are individually connected to a central connecting device such as a switch or hub.

questions.question: Which topology uses a single backbone cable to connect all devices?
questions.explanation: In a bus topology, all devices share a single communication line or backbone cable.

questions.question: In which topology is each device connected to exactly two other devices, forming a closed loop?
questions.explanation: In a ring topology, each node connects to exactly two neighboring nodes, forming a single continuous closed circular path.

questions.question: Which topology provides a dedicated point-to-point link between every pair of devices?
questions.explanation: A full mesh topology provides dedicated point-to-point connections between every pair of nodes on the network.

questions.question: If a network has 6 devices in a full mesh topology, how many links are required?
questions.explanation: Using the formula n(n - 1)/2: with n = 6, total links = 6(6 - 1)/2 = (6 × 5)/2 = 15 links.

questions.question: If 8 devices are connected using a full mesh topology, how many links are required?
questions.explanation: Using n(n - 1)/2 for n = 8: (8 × 7)/2 = 28 duplex physical links.

questions.question: What is the formula for the number of links in a full mesh network with n devices?
questions.explanation: The formula to determine the number of physical links in a fully connected mesh network of n devices is n(n - 1)/2.

questions.question: In a star topology, what happens if the central switch fails?
options: The entire network may become unavailable
The network automatically becomes a bus
questions.explanation: Because all nodes rely on the central hub or switch to communicate, failure of the central device creates a single point of failure that disables the entire network.

questions.question: Which topology has the highest redundancy and fault tolerance when every node is connected to every other node?
questions.explanation: A full mesh topology provides the highest fault tolerance and redundancy because multiple alternate paths exist between every pair of nodes.

questions.question: Which topology generally requires the least amount of cabling for connecting multiple devices?
questions.explanation: A bus topology requires the least cabling because all stations tap into a single shared backbone cable.

questions.question: Which topology has a hierarchical structure consisting of multiple levels of nodes?
questions.explanation: A tree topology features a hierarchical, branching structure with root, intermediate, and leaf nodes arranged in levels.

questions.question: A network combines two or more different types of topologies. What is it called?
questions.explanation: A hybrid topology integrates elements of two or more distinct topologies (e.g., star-bus or star-ring) into a unified network.

questions.question: Which topology is most vulnerable to failure of its single backbone cable?
questions.explanation: In a bus topology, a break or fault in the primary backbone cable halts all communication across the entire bus.

questions.question: In a ring topology with 10 devices, how many direct links are normally required to form the complete ring?
questions.explanation: In a standard single-ring topology with n devices, exactly n direct links are required to connect each node to its neighbor in a closed loop (10 devices = 10 links).

questions.question: In a full mesh topology with 10 devices, how many links are required?
questions.explanation: Applying n(n - 1)/2 with n = 10 gives 10(9)/2 = 45 total physical links.

questions.question: In a star topology with 12 devices connected to one central switch, how many direct links are required?
questions.explanation: In a star topology, each individual end device requires exactly one dedicated link to the central switch, resulting in 12 links for 12 devices.

questions.question: In a full mesh network of 7 devices, how many links must be added if one new device is introduced?
questions.explanation: To maintain full mesh connectivity, adding an 8th device requires establishing a new dedicated link to each of the 7 existing devices, so 7 links must be added.

questions.question: Which topology is commonly associated with token-based access mechanisms?
questions.explanation: Token Ring networks (IEEE 802.5) pass a small frame called a token circularly around the ring topology to control medium access.

questions.question: Which topology provides the greatest number of alternative paths between nodes?
questions.explanation: A full mesh topology provides direct dedicated paths as well as multiple alternate routing paths between all nodes.

questions.question: A network has 15 devices in a full mesh topology. How many total links are required?
questions.explanation: Using n(n - 1)/2 for n = 15: 15 × 14 / 2 = 105 total links.

questions.question: Which type of network typically covers a small geographical area such as a room, office, or building?
questions.explanation: A Local Area Network (LAN) covers a restricted geographic radius such as a single room, office, home, or commercial building.

questions.question: Which network is designed to cover a metropolitan or city-wide area?
questions.explanation: A Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) is designed to interconnect communication resources spanning an entire city or metropolitan region.

questions.question: Which type of network generally covers the largest geographical area?
questions.explanation: A Wide Area Network (WAN) spans the largest geographical area, interconnecting regions across cities, countries, or continents.

questions.question: Which network is primarily designed for communication among personal devices around an individual?
questions.explanation: A Personal Area Network (PAN) interconnects devices centered around an individual person within a short radius of a few meters.

questions.question: Bluetooth communication between a smartphone and a wireless headset is an example of:
questions.explanation: Short-range wireless connections between personal accessories like smartphones and headsets form a Personal Area Network (PAN).

questions.question: A network connecting computers within a university campus is generally classified as:
questions.explanation: Computers interconnected within a contiguous campus or organizational property are classified as a LAN (or Campus LAN).

questions.question: A network connecting multiple LANs across different branches within the same city is most appropriately classified as:
questions.explanation: Interconnecting disparate LANs distributed across municipal branch offices within a single city constitutes a Metropolitan Area Network (MAN).

questions.question: A company connects its offices in Dhaka, Chattogram, and Rajshahi using a private network. Which type of network is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: A network connecting distant branch offices located across different major cities and divisions of a country is a Wide Area Network (WAN).

questions.question: Which network usually has the smallest coverage area?
questions.explanation: A Personal Area Network (PAN) typically spans a workspace radius of approximately 10 meters, making it the smallest in geographical reach.

questions.question: Which network generally provides high-speed communication within a single building?
questions.explanation: A Local Area Network (LAN) delivers high-speed data transmission (e.g., Gigabit Ethernet) within a single facility or office building.

questions.question: Which network is commonly used to connect geographically distant cities or countries?
questions.explanation: Wide Area Networks (WANs) utilize long-distance telecommunication circuits to connect distant cities, states, and nations.

questions.question: A smartwatch communicating with a smartphone using Bluetooth forms a:
questions.explanation: Wearables communicating with mobile phones via Bluetooth operate within a personal operating space, forming a PAN.

questions.question: Which type of network is larger than a LAN but smaller than a WAN?
questions.explanation: A Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) bridges the scale between local area networks and wide area networks.

questions.question: The Internet is best described as an example of a:
questions.explanation: The global Internet is the quintessential example of a public Wide Area Network (WAN), interconnecting millions of smaller networks.

questions.question: Which network type is generally owned and controlled by a single organization within a limited area?
questions.explanation: LANs are typically privately owned, deployed, and managed by a single enterprise or entity across a localized premise.

questions.question: If 20 computers are connected within a single office using Ethernet switches, the network is most likely a:
questions.explanation: An interconnected cluster of office computers utilizing Ethernet switching within an office suite is a classic Local Area Network (LAN).

questions.question: Which network would be most suitable for connecting several government offices located throughout a city?
questions.explanation: Connecting distributed public administration offices across different zones of a municipality is the standard role of a MAN.

questions.question: Which technology is commonly associated with PAN connectivity?
questions.explanation: Bluetooth (IEEE 802.15.1) is the standard wireless protocol designed specifically for Personal Area Networks.

questions.question: Which network type usually involves service-provider infrastructure and long-distance communication links?
questions.explanation: WAN deployments depend on telecommunication carrier infrastructure, leased lines, and long-haul transmission systems.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly arranges these networks from smallest to largest typical geographical coverage?
questions.explanation: In order of physical scope: Personal Area Network (PAN) < Local Area Network (LAN) < Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) < Wide Area Network (WAN).

questions.question: How many usable host addresses are available in a /24 IPv4 network?
questions.explanation: A /24 network has 8 host bits (2^8 = 256 addresses). Subtracting the network address and broadcast address leaves 254 usable host addresses.

questions.question: What is the subnet mask for a /26 network?
How many usable host addresses are available in a /26 subnet?
questions.explanation: With a /26 prefix, 6 bits remain for hosts (32 - 26 = 6). Total addresses = 2^6 = 64; usable host addresses = 64 - 2 = 62.

questions.question: How many subnets are created when a /24 network is divided into /27 subnets?
questions.explanation: Borrowing bits from /24 to /27 yields 27 - 24 = 3 borrowed subnet bits. Number of subnets created = 2^3 = 8.

questions.question: How many usable hosts can a /27 subnet support?
questions.explanation: A /27 subnet leaves 32 - 27 = 5 host bits. Total addresses = 2^5 = 32; usable host addresses = 32 - 2 = 30.

questions.question: What is the subnet mask for /28?
questions.explanation: A /28 prefix has 4 bits on in the fourth octet: 11110000 binary = 128 + 64 + 32 + 16 = 240, giving 255.255.255.240.

questions.question: How many usable host addresses are available in a /28 subnet?
questions.explanation: A /28 subnet has 32 - 28 = 4 host bits. Total addresses = 2^4 = 16; usable hosts = 16 - 2 = 14.

questions.question: What is the block size of a /27 subnet in the last octet?
questions.explanation: The mask for /27 is 255.255.255.224. The block size (increment) is 256 - 224 = 32.

questions.question: What is the network address of 192.168.10.75/26?
questions.explanation: For /26 (mask 255.255.255.192), the block size is 64. Subnet ranges are 0-63, 64-127. Host .75 falls in the subnet starting at 192.168.10.64.

questions.question: What is the broadcast address of 192.168.10.75/26?
questions.explanation: The subnet range for 192.168.10.75/26 is 192.168.10.64 through 192.168.10.127, making 192.168.10.127 the directed broadcast address.
